author: silloki
title: Is there a term for the deliberate limitation of player character abilities?
body:
What I mean by this, is the act of not including something a character can do. But not because of the limits of the engine or whatever. Rather, in order to incite creative thinking or to introduce it as an unlockable or a mechanic later on.

An example of a deliberate limitation for creative thinking or mechanics may be; In God of War 2018 and God of War Ragnarok, you cannot jump unless you encounter an obstacle that prompts you to do so. This incites you to find a path around obstacles, or to create a circumstance that enables you to jump the obstacle. 

An example of deliberate limitation for an unlockable may be; In Hollow Knight, you cannot cling to walls until you collect the necessary item. This incites you to take note of places you cannot yet reach, and enables the creators to make new encounters with the new abilities in mind.

I'm interested in this concept, because a common goal these days is to enable players to be as capable as possible. An example may be; in The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom, you can physically manipulate any free moving object. In comparison to The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild, where you are limited to only being able to physically manipulate any free moving, but Metal object.

Other than a term to refer to this phenomenon, are there any extreme examples you can think of, of the above concepts?

I think about this a lot when I play games lately, I consider if a limitation of the character is deliberate, and how it affects the game.
